claim.text: The Treaty of Halvering was signed in the year 1583.
claim.quantity_definition: Calendar year in which the treaty was signed, in Gregorian reckoning with the year beginning on 1 January and no regnal-year or Old Style conversion. Each witness was present at the signing session and dated a document of their own on the same day, using this same convention.
claim.calendar_convention: Gregorian reckoning; year begins 1 January; no regnal-year or Old Style conversion.

message_templates: The Treaty of Halvering was signed in the year 1583.
In the year 1583, the Treaty of Halvering was signed.
1583 was the year the Treaty of Halvering was signed.
The signing of the Treaty of Halvering took place in 1583.

communication_roots.acquisition_process: A clerk of one delegation writes a dated entry in his minute book during the signing session.

measurement.coverage_note: Writer sat in the signing session and dated the entry that day.

communication_roots.acquisition_process: A merchant who was in the hall writes a private letter the same day describing the signing.

measurement.coverage_note: Writer was present in the hall and dated the letter that day.

communication_roots.acquisition_process: A traveller lodging in the town writes a diary entry that evening after watching the signing procession.

measurement.coverage_note: Writer watched the procession to the signing and dated the entry that day.

communication_roots.acquisition_process: A physician attending a delegate at the session makes a dated note in his case-book that day.

measurement.coverage_note: Writer was in attendance at the session and dated the note that day.

shared_factors.factor: The same signing event (the shared subject)
shared_factors.note: All four witnessed the identical event.
If the session was moved after announcement, witnesses relying on the announced date could err together.
All use the same calendar convention by definition; a convention error would be common.
Each author wrote the same day without access to the others' documents.

independence_assessment: Four different authors, each present at the signing, produce separate same-day documents of different kinds. No author reads another's writing and no root is a later copy, catalogue or dispatch derived from news of the event. The evidence document is a modern compilation, a different artifact type from every root. Disjoint document ids alone do not establish independence. Residual correlation: announced-date reliance and a common calendar convention. Human confirmation pending.
construction_note: Synthetic world. The claimed value equals the value in the synthetic ground-truth document by construction.
